submission.natural_language_explanation: L7/N499+ is a lexical detector for the English verb DO: it fires hardest on the token that carries DO's stem in any full surface form (' do'/'Do', ' does'/'Does', ' did'/'Did', ' doing', and 'done' when it is a verbal participle), no matter what role DO plays - auxiliary of negation ('they do not change', 3.9), emphatic verb ('They did experience', 3.6), inverted support in a wh-question whose subject precedes it ('subjects do you have', 3.6), imperative ('Do this', 3.8) or the main verb ('the filter does a good job', 3.9; 'were doing research', 3.8) - and it is indifferent to negation and to what follows ('does not' = 'does often' = 'does mention', all 3.5-3.6). It is not a general auxiliary, tense or negation detector: be/have/can/will/would/could/should/must sit at -0.12 mean over thousands of occurrences (max 0.52), ordinary verbs (mention, require, use, say) at about 0, and activation is graded down within the DO paradigm - to 0.2-0.3 when the same form is clause-initial/inverted rather than in its post-subject slot ('Why does this happen?' 0.26, 'and so does the assistant' 0.18, 'she wondered why does the manager...' 0.82 vs 2.79 in situ; across the scan mean 0.82 vs 2.36), to roughly half on the contraction stems don't/doesn't/didn't (mean 0.92-1.38 vs 2.1), and to ~0.3 on adjectival 'done' ('the job is done') though verbal 'has done' still reaches 3.1; the only fringe outside DO is the modal 'may' (mean 0.66, max 1.9), while the 'Am' entry in this pole's confound profile is a subword fragment of names ('Amstrong', 'Amish', 'Amro', 'Amazin') - the copula ' am' is flat at 0.11.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Same furnace-filter topic and negation frame as top example 4, but with 'can'/'cannot' instead of 'does'; the hypothesis puts can at the non-DO auxiliary baseline (max 0.52), so it predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Apologists have argued that the beginning of the universe has been established beyond doubt, and that the cosmological argument will settle the question.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same cosmological-apologetics topic as top example 3 with 'have', 'has been' and 'will' but no DO form; the hypothesis predicts be/have/will sit near -0.12.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Retreat of the ice shelf was not expected to change estimates of future sea level rise, and the authors were careful to say so.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Does the pressure valve need to be replaced before the inspection, or is a routine service enough?
adversarial_test_results.detail: Clause-initial inverted 'Does' in a yes/no question; the hypothesis explicitly grades clause-initial and inverted DO down to 0.2-0.3, so it predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The night manager checks every lock, and so do the cleaners before they leave.
adversarial_test_results.detail: VP-ellipsis 'so do' with the auxiliary inverted ahead of its subject; the hypothesis grades inverted support ('and so does the assistant' 0.18) down, so it predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Only after the third attempt did the auditors find the missing invoice in the archive.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Negative-adverb inversion 'Only after ... did the auditors': the hypothesis attributes the graded drop to inversion rather than to absolute sentence position, so it predicts no firing even with the trigger in mid-sentence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Patients may experience mild dizziness during the first week of treatment, and it usually fades without any change in dosage.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Modal 'may' in a medical context; the hypothesis calls may its only marginal fringe (mean 0.66, max 1.9) and denies being a general modal detector, so it predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I am quite sure the old bridge is safe, but the engineers want another survey before winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Copula 'am' (plus 'is') in a plain declarative; the hypothesis reports copula 'am' flat at 0.11 and explains the 'Am' confound as name fragments, so it predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At the end of a word, an unpaired consonant followed by a voiced consonant is pronounced voiceless; otherwise it is voiced. The letter в is not one of the paired consonants.

Every spring the city's public works department opens the reservoir spillway for a week and lets the excess meltwater run down the old stone channel toward the river. The channel was built in 1911 by crews who worked through two winters, and most of the original blockwork is still in place. Inspectors walk the length of it twice a year, checking for cracks, root intrusion and the slow settling that shows up first at the joints. What they find goes into a ledger that no one outside the department has read in decades.

The spillway itself is less impressive than the channel. It is a concrete lip about forty meters wide with steel gates that lift on chains, and when the gates open the water spreads into a thin sheet that catches the light. Children on the footbridge above it like to watch the foam pile up against the pilings. Fishermen below the bridge know the week the gates open better than anyone, because the current pushes baitfish downstream and the larger fish follow.

Downstream, the river narrows between two wooded banks before widening again into a shallow basin where herons and kingfishers hunt. The basin silts up every few years, and the department dredges it on a schedule that depends on the budget rather than on the silt. Last time the dredge was delayed by two summers, and by the third the boat launch at the north end was unusable. The county filed a complaint, the state sent an engineer, and the engineer's report recommended a settling pond upstream of the launch, which has not been built.

The department's own engineers are divided about the pond. One group argues that a settling pond would trap sediment before it reaches the basin and cut dredging costs by a third. Another group points out that the pond would need its own maintenance budget, and that a pond that silted up faster than predicted would simply move the problem upstream. Both groups agree that the current arrangement is expensive. Neither group can show what the other arrangement would cost, because the department has never tracked dredging costs by site.

The footbridge was repainted two summers ago in a colour the neighborhood association still complains about, and the contractor who painted it has since stopped returning calls. The association wants the railings a darker green, but the department has said that repainting is not in this year's budget and that the matter can wait until the channel is next inspected.

The ledger, it turns out, does track them, but only since 1998, and only in a column labeled 'misc.' that the finance office has interpreted differently in each of the last four audits. The city auditor's most recent memo asks for a consistent definition before the next budget cycle. The department has promised an answer by autumn. Meanwhile the gates will open again in April, the foam will pile up against the pilings, and the fishermen will be there before the inspectors are.

explanation_scores.explanation: L7/N499+ is a lexical detector for the English verb DO: it fires hardest on the token that carries DO's stem in any full surface form (' do'/'Do', ' does'/'Does', ' did'/'Did', ' doing', and 'done' when it is a verbal participle), no matter what role DO plays - auxiliary of negation ('they do not change', 3.9), emphatic verb ('They did experience', 3.6), inverted support in a wh-question whose subject precedes it ('subjects do you have', 3.6), imperative ('Do this', 3.8) or the main verb ('the filter does a good job', 3.9; 'were doing research', 3.8) - and it is indifferent to negation and to what follows ('does not' = 'does often' = 'does mention', all 3.5-3.6). It is not a general auxiliary, tense or negation detector: be/have/can/will/would/could/should/must sit at -0.12 mean over thousands of occurrences (max 0.52), ordinary verbs (mention, require, use, say) at about 0, and activation is graded down within the DO paradigm - to 0.2-0.3 when the same form is clause-initial/inverted rather than in its post-subject slot ('Why does this happen?' 0.26, 'and so does the assistant' 0.18, 'she wondered why does the manager...' 0.82 vs 2.79 in situ; across the scan mean 0.82 vs 2.36), to roughly half on the contraction stems don't/doesn't/didn't (mean 0.92-1.38 vs 2.1), and to ~0.3 on adjectival 'done' ('the job is done') though verbal 'has done' still reaches 3.1; the only fringe outside DO is the modal 'may' (mean 0.66, max 1.9), while the 'Am' entry in this pole's confound profile is a subword fragment of names ('Amstrong', 'Amish', 'Amro', 'Amazin') - the copula ' am' is flat at 0.11.
